items.prompt: A customer's order is 5 days late and they are frustrated. Write an email reply.

A customer emailed asking why their monthly subscription price rose by $4 this month. The increase comes from a plan-wide price change announced by email 30 days ago. Write a reply that explains the change, acknowledges their frustration, and sets out their options.
A customer ordered a blue jacket but received a black one. Write an email that apologizes, explains how they can return the wrong item at no cost, and confirms when the correct item will arrive.

A long-time customer wants to close their account because they found a cheaper competitor. Write a reply that thanks them for their loyalty, applies no pressure, and clearly explains how to cancel and what happens to their data.

A customer reports that your mobile app keeps logging them out. Engineering has confirmed the bug and expects a fix within a week. Write an email that acknowledges the problem, gives a realistic timeline, and offers a temporary workaround.

A customer is angry that they were charged twice for the same order. Write an email confirming you can see both charges, explaining that one will be refunded within five business days, and apologizing for the inconvenience.
A business customer has asked for a copy of an invoice from six months ago for their tax records. Write a short, professional email attaching the invoice and offering to send others if needed.

A customer left a one-star review saying support never replied to their earlier message. You have now found that message, which was missed. Write a reply that apologizes, addresses their original issue, and explains what you are doing to prevent a repeat.

A customer asks whether they can pause their subscription for three months while travelling instead of cancelling. Pausing is allowed for up to two months. Write a reply that explains the real policy and offers a workable alternative.
A customer's warranty claim has been approved. Write an email informing them, explaining that a replacement unit will ship in two days, and telling them how to return the faulty one.

A customer emailed asking for a feature your product does not have and may never build. Write a polite reply that thanks them, is honest that it is not on the roadmap, and explains how you will record their request.
A customer was promised a callback yesterday that never happened. Write an email that apologizes, briefly explains what went wrong internally, and offers two specific time slots for a call today.

A customer says a discount code from your newsletter did not work at checkout. The code expired two days before they tried it. Write a reply that explains this kindly and offers a one-time replacement code.
A customer has asked you to delete their personal data and close their account. Write a reply confirming you will do this, explaining the timeline, and noting anything they should download first.

A customer received a damaged package and has sent photos. Write an email thanking them for the photos, confirming a replacement at no charge, and explaining that they do not need to return the damaged item.

A customer is frustrated that your phone line had a 40-minute wait. Write an email that apologizes, explains that call volumes are unusually high this week, and points them to faster support channels.

A customer asks for a refund on a course they bought 45 days ago. Your refund window is 30 days. Write a reply that explains the policy clearly, shows empathy, and offers what help you can within the rules.

A customer's delivery has shown no movement in transit for five days. Write an email that acknowledges the delay, explains you have opened an investigation with the courier, and tells them what to expect next.
A new customer is confused about how to set up their account and has emailed for help. Write a friendly step-by-step reply that gets them started and invites them to reply if they get stuck.

A customer complains that an agent was abrupt with them on chat yesterday. Write an email that takes the complaint seriously, apologizes sincerely, and explains that you will follow up with the agent's manager.

A wholesale customer wants to increase their standing monthly order by 30% starting next month. Write a reply confirming you can do this, noting any change to pricing or lead time, and asking for written confirmation.
A customer asks whether your product is compatible with a device you have not tested. Write an honest reply that explains what you do and do not know and offers a safe way for them to try it.
A customer paid for express shipping but the order arrived by standard post. Write an email that apologizes, confirms a refund of the express fee, and explains how the mistake happened.

A customer wants to transfer their subscription to a colleague who is taking over their role. Write a reply explaining the steps, what information you need, and how billing will be handled during the switch.
A customer has emailed to say thank you after an agent helped them recover a lost file. Write a warm reply that acknowledges their message and passes the praise on to the agent.

A customer reports being locked out of their account after several failed login attempts. Write an email explaining the security lock, how long it lasts, and how they can safely reset their password now.

A customer is unhappy that a product they bought two weeks ago is now on sale for 25% less. You do not offer price adjustments. Write a reply that explains this politely and mentions how they can hear about future sales early.

A customer has asked for an update on a bug they reported a month ago that is still not fixed. Write an honest email explaining where the fix stands, why it has taken time, and when you expect it to be resolved.

A customer wants to return an opened software box for a refund. Opened software is non-refundable, but you can offer store credit. Write a reply that explains the policy and the credit option clearly and without blame.

A customer emailed the wrong department about a billing error. Write a brief, helpful reply that acknowledges their message, tells them you have forwarded it to billing, and sets expectations for when billing will respond.

items.reference_text: Thank you for calling our support line. I understand how frustrating a delayed delivery can be, and I want to make this right for you. Let me look into your order right now and find the fastest way to get it to you.

items.prompt: A customer calls to say a product they ordered arrived broken and they are upset. Walk me through, step by step, how you would handle this call from the moment you pick up to how you would resolve it.

items.reference_text: Thanks for reaching out today. I can see your order left our warehouse yesterday afternoon, and the tracking page should update within a few hours. If it hasn't moved by tomorrow morning, just reply here and I'll open a trace with the courier.

I'm sorry the setup wasn't as smooth as it should have been. Let's fix this together. First, please close the app completely, then open it again and sign in. Once you're back on the home screen, tell me what you see.

Good afternoon, and thank you for your patience while I looked into this. Your account is active again, and the double charge from Monday has been refunded. It usually takes three to five business days to appear, depending on your bank.

I completely understand why this is frustrating, and I want to get it sorted for you today. I've escalated your case to our senior team, and someone will call you within two hours. If you miss it, they'll leave a direct number.

Welcome, and thanks for choosing us. Your subscription starts today and renews on the same date each month. You can change your plan, update your card, or pause your account at any time from the billing page. Let me know if you need help.

I'm sorry to hear the part arrived damaged. You don't need to send anything back. I've arranged a replacement that ships tomorrow with next-day delivery, and I'll email the tracking number as soon as it's ready. Again, I apologise for the trouble.

Thank you for letting us know about the website error. Our engineers have confirmed the problem and expect a fix within a week. In the meantime, you can complete your purchase through the mobile app, and everything will sync automatically once you're back online.

I appreciate you taking the time to explain what happened. That's not the experience we want you to have, and I'm sorry. I've made a note on your account, shared your feedback with the team, and added a credit for this month.

Let me confirm the details before we continue. I have your order number, the email on file, and the delivery address, and everything matches what I'm seeing here. I'll process the change now, and you'll receive a confirmation message within a few minutes.

Your warranty claim has been approved, so there's nothing more you need to do on your side. A new unit will arrive within two working days, and a prepaid return label is included in the box for the faulty one.

I know waiting on hold isn't how anyone wants to spend their afternoon, and I'm sorry it took so long to reach us. Call volumes have been unusually high this week. For quicker help next time, our live chat is answered within minutes.

Here's what happens next. I'll send your request to our billing team today, and they'll review the charge and reply within one business day. If they need anything else from you, they'll ask by email rather than calling.

items.prompt: A customer says the same charge appears twice on their card and they want it fixed immediately. Walk me through, step by step, how you would confirm what happened and how you would explain the next steps to the customer.

A customer asks for a refund on a purchase made outside the refund window. Explain how you would handle the conversation, and justify how you would balance the company's policy against keeping the customer satisfied.
A new customer emails saying they cannot get the product to work and are close to giving up. Walk me through how you would guide them through the setup and keep them calm while you do it.
A customer is angry that a promised callback never happened. Explain how you would open the conversation, what you would say about the mistake, and how you would work to rebuild their trust.
Your company has just changed its return policy and customers are unhappy. Walk me through how you would explain the change to a customer on the phone and how you would respond to their objections.
A customer asks for a feature the product does not have and is unlikely to build. Explain how you would respond honestly without losing the customer, and justify the approach you would take.
A customer's delivery has been stuck in transit for a week with no updates. Walk me through, from the start of the call, how you would investigate and what you would commit to before hanging up.
A customer complains that one of your colleagues was rude to them yesterday. Explain how you would handle this call and what you would do afterwards, and justify why you would take those steps.
A customer is choosing between two of your subscription plans and is unsure which fits their needs. Walk me through the questions you would ask and how you would guide them toward a decision.
A customer reports a bug that engineering has known about for a month and still has not fixed. Explain how you would give them an honest update while keeping the relationship positive.
A long-time customer says they are cancelling because a competitor is cheaper. Walk me through how you would respond, and justify how far you would go to keep them.
A customer received the wrong item in their order. Walk me through, step by step, how you would apologise, arrange the correction, and make sure it does not happen again.
